## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

사용자가 원하는 건 인터랙션이 끝난 후에 스크롤을 한 번 더 해야 다음 섹션으로 넘어가는 거네.

# Frontend Rules

- Bundler: Vite / Language: TypeScript (ES6+)
- 3D: Three.js. Main scenes use `core/Engine.ts`; works scatter is the standalone secondary renderer in `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`.
- **Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`**
  - Reason: Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-bundles on every file save
  - Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency
  - Do not include these commands in verification steps, PR notes, or agent plans

## TypeScript

- All shared types/interfaces/enums live in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`; avoid inline exported types and `any`.
- Shared constants, colors, sizes, URLs, selectors, and timings live in `resource/ts/config/*.config.ts` or page scene config files.
- Page theatre: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Page scene/config composition: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Page-only lifecycle/runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`
- Standalone page renderer exception: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/render/` (currently works scatter)
- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.

## Three.js

- `dispose()` required for every geometry, material, texture, render target, and standalone renderer.
- Main WebGL renderer ownership belongs to `Engine`; standalone secondary renderers must call `renderer.dispose()` and `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- No object creation inside render loops or RAF hot paths.
- `addEventListener` must have matching `removeEventListener`.
- No monkey-patching Three.js API.

# SCSS Rules

- BEM pattern for class naming
- Source: `resource/scss/` → output: `resource/dist/`
- Do NOT run build commands — dev server reflects changes on save automatically
- Admin CSS (`admin/resource/css/`) is separate — do not import from public SCSS entry

## Token Contract

- Reusable tokens → `resource/scss/abstract/` or `base/_root.scss`
- Use `var(--clr-*)`, `var(--duration-*)` etc. in consumers — no raw hex when a semantic token exists upstream
- Prefer semantic tokens over raw values when an upstream token exists
- **Do NOT use CSS variable fallbacks** like `var(--token, fallback)`. Use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly.
- Do not introduce base/root tokens for one-off component values — only when genuinely shared across multiple features

## Fluid Helper

- In **component, layout, page** SCSS: call `fluid(min, max)` directly
- In shared **`abstract/`** or **`base/`**: use `#{fluid(...)}` interpolation only when emitting CSS custom properties or shared tokens
- Files outside `resource/scss/abstract/` and `resource/scss/base/`: add `@use "../abstract" as *;` at top before using `fluid(...)` and other shared helpers

## Reset / Init Contract

`_init.scss`가 다음을 전역 적용함 — 컴포넌트/페이지 SCSS에서 단독 중복 선언 금지:
- `margin: 0` → `*` selector로 이미 0
- `padding: 0` → `*` selector로 이미 0
- `list-style: none` → `ul, ol, li`에 이미 없음
- `padding-left: 0` / `padding-right: 0` 등 단일 축 0도 동일하게 금지
  (단, 직상위 규칙에서 해당 축에 non-zero 값이 선언되어 있으면 예외)

`@include font("...")` mixin은 `font-size`, `line-height`, `letter-spacing`을 모두 출력함.
mixin 호출 직후 동일 값으로 개별 재선언하지 않는다.

## 실제 원인 — 3가지 복합 문제

### 1. 가장 근본적 원인: 0.55 → 0.60 간격이 **5% = 10svh**밖에 안 됨

`scrollSpanVh: 200`에서 5% = **10svh**. 보통 스크롤 속도로 0.5~1초면 통과.

```
headline hide trigger (0.55)
  ↓ [10svh = 0.5초 스크롤]
sub timer start (0.60)
  ↓ [700ms]
sub 등장

헤드라인 CSS fade: 0.6s (--transition-slow)
→ sub 등장 시 헤드라인이 fade-out 진행 중 (overlap!)
```

### 2. `sHide` 조건의 구멍

```ts
const sHide = !sShow && progress < PROOF_STAGE_SPLIT;  // < 0.55
```

sub가 **show되는 threshold는 0.60**인데, **hide 조건은 0.55**. 0.55~0.60 구간에서 `sShow=false, sHide=false` → **sub가 visible 상태면 그대로 유지**.

→ 역방향 스크롤 시 0.55에서 headline이 다시 나오려 할 때 sub도 같은 위치에서 남아 있음.

### 3. 700ms delay의 기산점 오류

delay가 **headline가 hide되는 순간(0.55)**이 아니라 **sub threshold에 도달하는 순간(0.60)**부터 시작. 빠른 스크롤일수록 이 차이가 없어짐.

---

`PROOF_STAGE_SPLIT = 0.42`, `PROOF_SUB_SHOW = 0.68` — 간격을 **26% = 52svh**로 넓힘. delay를 `900ms`로 올리고 `sHide` 범위도 교정합니다.

# Frontend Rules

- Bundler: Vite / Language: TypeScript (ES6+)
- 3D: Three.js. Main scenes use `core/Engine.ts`; works scatter is the standalone secondary renderer in `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`.
- **Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`**
  - Reason: Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-bundles on every file save
  - Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency
  - Do not include these commands in verification steps, PR notes, or agent plans

## TypeScript

- All shared types/interfaces/enums live in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`; avoid inline exported types and `any`.
- Shared constants, colors, sizes, URLs, selectors, and timings live in `resource/ts/config/*.config.ts` or page scene config files.
- Page theatre: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Page scene/config composition: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Page-only lifecycle/runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`
- Standalone page renderer exception: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/render/` (currently works scatter)
- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.

## Three.js

- `dispose()` required for every geometry, material, texture, render target, and standalone renderer.
- Main WebGL renderer ownership belongs to `Engine`; standalone secondary renderers must call `renderer.dispose()` and `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- No object creation inside render loops or RAF hot paths.
- `addEventListener` must have matching `removeEventListener`.
- No monkey-patching Three.js API.

# SCSS Rules

- BEM pattern for class naming
- Source: `resource/scss/` → output: `resource/dist/`
- Do NOT run build commands — dev server reflects changes on save automatically
- Admin CSS (`admin/resource/css/`) is separate — do not import from public SCSS entry

## Token Contract

- Reusable tokens → `resource/scss/abstract/` or `base/_root.scss`
- Use `var(--clr-*)`, `var(--duration-*)` etc. in consumers — no raw hex when a semantic token exists upstream
- Prefer semantic tokens over raw values when an upstream token exists
- **Do NOT use CSS variable fallbacks** like `var(--token, fallback)`. Use `var(--token)` or `fluid(...)` directly.
- Do not introduce base/root tokens for one-off component values — only when genuinely shared across multiple features

## Fluid Helper

- In **component, layout, page** SCSS: call `fluid(min, max)` directly
- In shared **`abstract/`** or **`base/`**: use `#{fluid(...)}` interpolation only when emitting CSS custom properties or shared tokens
- Files outside `resource/scss/abstract/` and `resource/scss/base/`: add `@use "../abstract" as *;` at top before using `fluid(...)` and other shared helpers

## Reset / Init Contract

`_init.scss`가 다음을 전역 적용함 — 컴포넌트/페이지 SCSS에서 단독 중복 선언 금지:
- `margin: 0` → `*` selector로 이미 0
- `padding: 0` → `*` selector로 이미 0
- `list-style: none` → `ul, ol, li`에 이미 없음
- `padding-left: 0` / `padding-right: 0` 등 단일 축 0도 동일하게 금지
  (단, 직상위 규칙에서 해당 축에 non-zero 값이 선언되어 있으면 예외)

`@include font("...")` mixin은 `font-size`, `line-height`, `letter-spacing`을 모두 출력함.
mixin 호출 직후 동일 값으로 개별 재선언하지 않는다.

All changes are in place and TypeScript is clean. Here's what was done:

**HTML** ([views/pages/about/index.php](views/pages/about/index.php)): Replaced the flat `__sticky` + `__content` structure with two independent `__scene` > `__pin` > `__headline` wrappers. Each scene is its own scroll zone.

**SCSS** ([resource/scss/pages/_sub.scss](resource/scss/pages/_sub.scss)):
- Section: `height: 500svh` (fixed, not `min-height`)
- `__canvas-wrap`: `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` — ring canvas pins for the full 500svh
- `__scenes`: `position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 2` — overlay covering entire section
- `__scene`: `height: 200svh` — each text zone takes 200svh; two scenes = 400svh + 100svh buffer at end
- `__pin`: `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` — text sticks at top for the first 100svh of its scene, then naturally scrolls off

**Scroll behavior**: Text 1 is pinned at top for scene 1's first 100svh → scrolls off → 100svh gap → Text 2 pins for scene 2's first 100svh → scrolls off → 100svh hold buffer → section exits.

**TS** ([resource/ts/pages/about/scene/about.scene.ts](resource/ts/pages/about/scene/about.scene.ts)): Removed all threshold/timer/state logic for proof text. Proof handler now only forwards `_proofProgressCallback`.

**TS** ([resource/ts/pages/about/runtime/AboutPageRuntime.ts](resource/ts/pages/about/runtime/AboutPageRuntime.ts)): Added `IntersectionObserver` on each `__scene` — when a scene enters the viewport, `is-block-reveal-up` is toggled on its headline (triggering the existing blur/fade-up CSS transition). Ordering is guaranteed by scroll position: scene 1 exits before scene 2 enters.

# Frontend Rules

- Bundler: Vite / Language: TypeScript (ES6+)
- 3D: Three.js. Main scenes use `core/Engine.ts`; works scatter is the standalone secondary renderer in `pages/works/render/WorksSceneManager.ts`.
- **Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run watch`, or `npm install`**
  - Reason: Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-bundles on every file save
  - Only `npm install <package>` is allowed when adding a new dependency
  - Do not include these commands in verification steps, PR notes, or agent plans

## TypeScript

- All shared types/interfaces/enums live in `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`; avoid inline exported types and `any`.
- Shared constants, colors, sizes, URLs, selectors, and timings live in `resource/ts/config/*.config.ts` or page scene config files.
- Page theatre: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Page scene/config composition: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Page-only lifecycle/runtime: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/runtime/`
- Standalone page renderer exception: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/render/` (currently works scatter)
- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.

## Three.js

- `dispose()` required for every geometry, material, texture, render target, and standalone renderer.
- Main WebGL renderer ownership belongs to `Engine`; standalone secondary renderers must call `renderer.dispose()` and `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- No object creation inside render loops or RAF hot paths.
- `addEventListener` must have matching `removeEventListener`.
- No monkey-patching Three.js API.

content.text:
Clean. Here's what changed:

**Proof canvas (priority sort):**

`selectProofItems()` in [AboutProofRenderer.ts](resource/ts/pages/about/render/AboutProofRenderer.ts) builds the ring card list in this order:
1. `is_awarded='Y'` + has video → first (most prominent)
2. If total < 8: `is_awarded='Y'` + no video → fill with image fallback
3. If still < 8: `대기업` (category=1) works with video → supplement
Per-card texture: `thumbnailVideo` → VideoTexture, else `fileAttach1 || thumbnailImage`.

API change ([api/works.php](api/works.php)): `is_awarded` now selected in list query and exposed as `isAwarded: boolean` in response. Types updated in [work.types.ts](resource/ts/types/work.types.ts).

**Gallery canvas (bigger + more motion):**

[InfiniteGalleryRenderer.ts](resource/ts/pages/about/render/InfiniteGalleryRenderer.ts):
- Scale: `2` → `4` (planes 2× bigger — fills ~30–38% of screen at typical depth)
- `SCROLL_SPEED`: `1.0` → `2.5` (scroll input 2.5× more sensitive)
- `AUTO_PLAY_ACCEL`: `0.3` → `0.7` (faster autoplay sweep)
- `MAX_SCROLL_VEL`: `20.0` → `40.0` (higher top speed cap)
